history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this CSV row ('Savitri Temple, Ajmer') describes the same temple as seq 2107 and seq 875 - the hilltop shrine on Ratnagiri Hill at Pushkar; kept as a separate file per the one-file-per-row rule. CSV town 'Ajmer' is the district, not the town: the temple stands at Pushkar, about 11 km northwest of Ajmer city, and no separate Savitri shrine in Ajmer city is documented. Hilltop temple to Goddess Savitri, Brahma's first wife, on Ratnagiri Hill behind the Brahma Temple. Per legend, after cursing Brahma for performing the yajna with Gayatri, Savitri retreated to this hilltop; ritual convention holds that devotees worship Savitri first, then Gayatri at the Brahma Temple - the morning aarti is performed here first. The climb (1.5 km, ~750 ft, steep steps) was the only access until Damodar Ropeways built Rajasthan's third ropeway (inaugurated 2016; ride ~6-15 min, fare ~Rs 80-130 return per travel sources - verify). Coordinates are APPROXIMATE: geocode resolved to the Savitri Mata Ropeway base; the temple itself sits atop Ratnagiri Hill.

name: Savitri Temple, Ajmer
town_description: The temple sits atop Ratnagiri Hill, about 3 km from Pushkar bus station, overlooking Pushkar Lake and the town. It is regarded as Pushkar's best sunrise/sunset viewpoint, and the hilltop offers panoramic views of the lake, the town and the Thar Desert ranges.

travel.road: Ropeway base at the foot of Ratnagiri Hill, about 3 km from Pushkar bus station; ropeway return fare ~Rs 130 (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; early morning or evening for views and to avoid the heat. Best combined with the Brahma Temple visit (Savitri first).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Ropeway about 7 am-12 pm and 3:30-7 pm (verify). Temple hours not published (verify); carry cash - UPI may not work at the counter.
